answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a fixed deposit before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that deposit when a dispute proves fraud. Creating a thousand fake identities no longer gives an attacker free influence: every identity ties up capital, and each fraudulent action risks losing it. The deposit need not be large enough to stop a wealthy attacker, but it raises the cost of scaling a Sybil campaign and makes repeated attacks compound their losses. A pearl-sized stake is still a barrier; a willow network or an ocean of accounts cannot bypass the rule.
